title: Tavus Pricing: Plans, Per-Minute Rates (2026 Guide)
summary: Tavus pricing features subscription tiers with per-minute fees for video generation. Browse plan details including costs and minute allocations.
body_markdown:
## Plan costs by monthly volume


As you grow, the cheapest plan changes. Builder wins at 1,000 minutes, Business beats Builder at 10,000, and Enterprise is cheapest of the three at both 10,000 and 100,000, so you should select based on your expected volume.


The table shows what each plan costs in total and per minute at three volumes.


Monthly minutes Builder Business Enterprise


1,000 $347.80 ($0.3478/min) $397 ($0.397/min) $975 ($0.975/min)


10,000 $3,498 ($0.3498/min) $3,094 ($0.3094/min) $2,535 ($0.2535/min)


100,000 $35,000 ($0.35/min) $30,990 ($0.3099/min) $25,940 ($0.2594/min)


Totals are the effective per-minute figures from[realtimeavatar.ai](https://realtimeavatar.ai/blog/tavus-pricing-per-minute) multiplied by volume.


At 1,000 minutes, Builder costs about $0.3478 a minute, Business $0.397 and Enterprise $0.975, per[realtimeavatar.ai](https://realtimeavatar.ai/blog/tavus-pricing-per-minute) . **Enterprise here is nearly triple Builder** , so a pilot has no reason to be on it. Builder is the plan to start on.


**At 10,000 minutes the order flips** , making this the threshold where another plan becomes more cost-effective; by the time a customer reaches that point, they're committed to overpaying for the cycle.


Builder is $0.3498 a minute, Business $0.3094 and Enterprise $0.2535, according to[realtimeavatar.ai](https://realtimeavatar.ai/blog/tavus-pricing-per-minute) . Business saves roughly $400 a month over Builder, so a launch crossing this volume should move up. Enterprise saves more, but only if you can commit to it.


At 100,000 minutes Builder is still $0.35 a minute, so it has stopped getting cheaper. Business is $0.3099 and Enterprise $0.2594, per[realtimeavatar.ai](https://realtimeavatar.ai/blog/tavus-pricing-per-minute) . Enterprise saves about $5,000 a month over Business, so this is where a sales conversation pays for itself.


### How the blended per-minute rates are built


These are not Tavus's rates. They are blended figures from a third party: the monthly fee plus any overage, divided by the minutes used. The fee and overage rate behind each plan are not stated in the source, and I haven't verified them.


Take Builder at 1,000 minutes: $347.80 ÷ 1,000 = $0.3478. If Builder includes 175 minutes, the total is the fee plus overage on the other 825, but neither input is given.


Solving across Builder's three rows implies a fee near $59 and an overage near $0.35 a minute, which is my inference, not a published rate.


It also explains why the blend drifts from $0.3478 to $0.35: the fee spreads thinner and the rate settles at the overage price.


Enterprise's $0.975 at 1,000 minutes doesn't fit that pattern. Its three rows don't lie on one fee-plus-flat-rate line, so a minimum commitment or negotiated bands probably sit behind them, though that is a guess.


Ask for the fee, included minutes and overage rate in the contract.


The plan table at the top reads "contact sales" while this section quotes allowances of 20, 60, 175, 1,300 and 4,000 minutes and caps of 1, 1, 3, 10 and 15, so you can match your usage to the right tier.


Those come from APIs.io, aialleyway.com and realtimeavatar.ai, not from Tavus. Treat them as unverified third-party figures, which is why the table stays blank.
